question: A pair of earrings is bought for ₹27,650 and is sold at a profit of 5%. Find the profit (in ₹). (Round off your answer to the nearest rupee)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit = 5% of Cost Price

Profit = 5% × 27,650

Profit = 27,650 ÷ 20 = 1,382.50

Rounding off 1,382.50 to the nearest rupee → 1,383

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,383.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹27,650

Profit Percentage = 5%

**Formula Used:**

Profit = (Profit% ÷ 100) × Cost Price

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6ba2dc359355d85b3de176d6700c8ea8bf2baa3a388b301c089a4dd9bedc7d65.png] 

⇒ Profit = (5 ÷ 100) × 27,650

⇒ Profit = 0.05 × 27,650

⇒ Profit = 1,382.5

⇒ Rounding off to the nearest rupee ≈ 1,383

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,383.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Selling Price Formula

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%)/100. In case of loss, SP = CP × (100 − Loss%)/100.

Profit Percentage

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100. Always calculate profit and loss percentages on the Cost Price unless specified otherwise.

Successive Discounts

The effective discount for two successive discounts a% and b% is given by (a + b − ab/100)%.

2f:T
